stage_projects.name: Raw Node HTTP File Server
stage_projects.description: A file server built with zero frameworks using only the Node.js http module — routing, static file serving, and JSON responses hand-rolled — to understand what Express actually abstracts away. Domain: systems/infra fundamentals.

stage_projects.name: Bookstore REST API with Express
stage_projects.description: A clean Express-based REST API (CRUD for books, authors, categories) with proper middleware layering, route organization, and centralized error handling. Domain: retail/inventory.

stage_projects.name: Pluggable Middleware Pipeline Framework
stage_projects.description: Build a tiny Express-compatible middleware pipeline from scratch (your own mini-framework mimicking app.use()/next()) to fully understand the middleware pattern, then reimplement one real feature (logging) both in your framework and in real Express side-by-side. Domain: framework/systems engineering.

stage_projects.name: Public API with Rate Limiting & CORS Policy
stage_projects.description: A small public-facing API (e.g., a quotes/jokes API) with a documented CORS policy, express-rate-limit tuned per endpoint tier (free vs authenticated), and async error handling via express-async-errors so no unhandled rejection crashes the server. Domain: public API products. A comment/review submission API where all HTML input is sanitized server-side with DOMPurify (server-side variant) before storage, with a deliberate XSS payload test suite proving the sanitization actually works. Domain: content platforms / trust & safety.

stage_projects.name: Hardened Production API Checklist Implementation
stage_projects.description: Take an existing API and harden it end-to-end: Helmet.js security headers, response compression, tuned CORS, rate limiting by IP and by API key, and a written security checklist with before/after header comparison (via curl -I). Domain: security engineering / SRE.

stage_projects.name: Full Supertest Suite for the Bookstore API
stage_projects.description: A comprehensive Supertest test suite for the Stage 1 Bookstore API covering happy paths, validation failures, auth-protected routes, and edge cases (empty body, malformed JSON, huge payloads). Domain: QA engineering.

stage_projects.name: Normalized Multi-Tenant Schema Design
stage_projects.description: Design and implement (via Prisma migrations) a normalized PostgreSQL schema for a multi-tenant SaaS (organizations, users, projects, roles) with correct foreign keys and cascade rules. Domain: B2B SaaS.

stage_projects.name: Serverless Postgres Comparison Project
stage_projects.description: Deploy the same schema/API to both Supabase and Neon, documenting connection pooling differences, cold-start behavior, and pricing/scaling tradeoffs from hands-on testing. Domain: infrastructure decision-making.

stage_projects.name: Slow Query Detective Agency
stage_projects.description: Given a seeded database with 1M+ rows and a set of deliberately slow endpoints, use EXPLAIN ANALYZE to diagnose each bottleneck, apply the correct fix (index, query restructure, N+1 fix via Prisma include), and document before/after query plans and timings. Domain: database performance engineering.

stage_projects.name: From-Scratch Password Auth
stage_projects.description: A signup/login system built without an auth-as-a-service library: bcrypt for hashing, JWT access tokens, httpOnly refresh-token cookies with SameSite=Lax, and a documented token-rotation strategy. Domain: security engineering / any product needing custom auth. A small service that receives webhooks (simulate a payment provider) and verifies HMAC-SHA256 signatures before trusting the payload, including a deliberate test proving a tampered payload is rejected. Domain: payments/fintech infrastructure.

stage_projects.name: jose-Based Multi-Audience Token System
stage_projects.description: A token system using the jose library supporting multiple audiences (web client, mobile client, internal service-to-service) with different expiry/claims per audience, and a key-rotation mechanism (JWKS-style) so old tokens gracefully expire during a key rotation. Domain: platform/identity engineering.

stage_projects.name: Fully-Tested Utility Library
stage_projects.description: Take a utility library from an earlier phase and bring it to 100% meaningful coverage with Vitest, including edge cases, with a coverage report published via Codecov. Domain: dev tooling.

stage_projects.name: Mocked API Component Test Suite
stage_projects.description: A React component suite (forms, data tables) tested with React Testing Library + @testing-library/user-event for realistic interactions, and MSW to mock network requests so tests never hit a real backend. Domain: frontend QA.

stage_projects.name: Regression-Proof Checkout Flow Tests
stage_projects.description: A full test suite for a multi-step checkout component (from Phase 4’s state machine work) covering every state transition, error path, and MSW-simulated payment failure, with coverage thresholds enforced in CI and tracked over time in Codecov. Domain: e-commerce QA engineering.

stage_projects.name: Critical User Journey E2E Suite
stage_projects.description: Playwright tests covering the 3 most critical user journeys of any earlier full-stack project (signup → login → core action), running against a real (test) database. Domain: QA engineering.

stage_projects.name: Cross-Browser Visual Regression Suite
stage_projects.description: Playwright tests that run across Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit, include visual snapshot comparisons for key pages, and are wired to fail CI on unexpected visual diffs. Domain: QA / design systems.

stage_projects.name: Matrix-Tested Cross-Version CI
stage_projects.description: A CI workflow using a build matrix to test a library across multiple Node.js versions and operating systems simultaneously, with a status badge reflecting real pass/fail state. Domain: open-source maintenance / library engineering.

stage_projects.name: Multi-Stage Dockerized Full-Stack App
stage_projects.description: Dockerize a full-stack app (Phase 5 backend + a frontend build) using multi-stage builds to keep the final image small, with a documented image-size before/after comparison. Domain: DevOps.

stage_projects.name: Local Dev Environment via Docker Compose
stage_projects.description: A docker-compose.yml that spins up the app, a Postgres database, and Redis together with one command, including healthchecks and proper service dependency ordering. Domain: developer experience / infra.

stage_projects.name: Automated Image Publishing Pipeline
stage_projects.description: A GitHub Actions workflow using docker/build-push-action to build and publish a versioned, tagged image to GitHub Container Registry on every merge to main, including a documented rollback procedure using a previous tag. Domain: DevOps / release engineering.

stage_projects.name: HTTP/2 Performance Verification
stage_projects.description: Deploy the same app behind both HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 configurations (or verify Render’s default) and document real measured differences in multiplexed asset loading via browser waterfall charts. Domain: web performance / infra.

stage_projects.name: Cross-Platform Habit Tracker
stage_projects.description: Rebuild Phase 2’s habit tracker as a React Native + Expo app, documenting layout differences (Flexbox defaults differ from web) and navigation using React Navigation (stack + tabs). Domain: personal wellness / mobile.

stage_projects.name: Recipe Browser with Deep Linking
stage_projects.description: A recipe browsing app with nested navigation (stack inside tabs), deep linking support (opening a specific recipe from a shared URL), and platform-aware layout adjustments for notches/safe areas. Domain: lifestyle/food.

stage_projects.name: EAS-Built Multi-Environment App
stage_projects.description: An app configured with separate dev/staging/production build profiles via EAS Build, each pointing to a different API environment, with a documented build-and-distribute workflow for internal testers. Domain: mobile release engineering.

stage_projects.name: Offline-First Grocery List
stage_projects.description: A grocery list app that works fully offline using AsyncStorage, queues changes made offline, and syncs to a backend when connectivity returns, with conflict resolution for simultaneous edits. Domain: productivity / offline-first apps. A mobile login flow storing tokens in expo-secure-store (not AsyncStorage) with biometric-gated access to sensitive actions, and a documented threat-model comparison of AsyncStorage vs. secure-store. Domain: mobile security.

stage_projects.name: Receipt Scanner Utility
stage_projects.description: An app using the camera API to photograph receipts, request the correct permissions gracefully (with a fallback UI if denied), and save images locally. Domain: personal finance / utility apps. A reminders app sending real push notifications (via Expo push service) with platform-specific permission flows for iOS vs Android documented and handled distinctly. Domain: productivity.

stage_projects.name: 10,000-Item Contact List
stage_projects.description: A contacts app rendering a very large list using FlatList performance best practices (getItemLayout, windowing tuning) profiled before/after optimization. Domain: productivity / performance engineering.

stage_projects.name: Hermes vs JSC Benchmark Report
stage_projects.description: Build a CPU-intensive screen (e.g., client-side image filtering) and benchmark its performance under the Hermes engine vs JSC, documenting startup time and runtime differences with real numbers. Domain: mobile performance engineering.

stage_projects.name: Zero-Downtime OTA Update Demo
stage_projects.description: Ship a bug fix to a live-installed app using EAS Update (over-the-air) without requiring users to redownload from the store, with a before/after demonstration and a documented rollback plan if the OTA update itself is broken. Domain: mobile release engineering.

stage_projects.name: Zero-GUI API Debugging Toolkit
stage_projects.description: A personal collection of curl scripts (with a Makefile or shell aliases) that fully exercise every endpoint of an earlier project’s API, usable by teammates with no GUI tool installed. Domain: developer tooling.

stage_projects.name: Shared Postman Collection with Environments
stage_projects.description: A Postman collection for a full-stack project with dev/staging/prod environments, pre-request scripts for auth token refresh, and automated test assertions per request, exported and version-controlled alongside the code. Domain: API QA/tooling.

stage_projects.name: Auto-Generated OpenAPI Docs Site
stage_projects.description: Write a complete OpenAPI 3.0 spec for an earlier project’s API by hand, render it with Swagger UI, and verify every documented example actually matches real API behavior (no doc drift). Domain: API developer experience.

stage_projects.name: Architecture Diagrams as Code
stage_projects.description: Document a full-stack project’s system architecture (request flow, database relationships, deployment topology) entirely using Mermaid diagrams embedded in markdown, version-controlled alongside the code. Domain: technical documentation / architecture.

stage_projects.name: Public-Facing Developer Portal
stage_projects.description: A polished, standalone documentation site for a public API combining OpenAPI-generated Swagger UI, hand-written getting-started guides, and Mermaid sequence diagrams showing common integration flows (e.g., OAuth handshake). Domain: developer relations / API products.

stage_projects.name: Blog GraphQL API
stage_projects.description: A GraphQL API (posts, authors, comments) with proper resolver structure, demonstrating the N+1 problem occurring naturally, then fixed with DataLoader-style batching. Domain: publishing/content. Implement the identical feature (a nested product/reviews/author data fetch) as both a REST endpoint and a GraphQL query, measuring over-fetching/under-fetching and request-count differences with real network data, and write a decision-framework document for when to choose each. Domain: API architecture.

stage_projects.name: Federated Multi-Service GraphQL Gateway
stage_projects.description: Split a schema across 2 independent services (e.g., Users service and Orders service) and compose them behind a single gateway, demonstrating schema federation concepts. Domain: microservices/API architecture.

stage_projects.name: Pattern Recognition Drill Set
stage_projects.description: Solve and document 8 problems each for Two Pointers and Sliding Window (16 total) from a mix of easy/medium difficulty, with a personal "pattern recognition cheat sheet" written afterward describing the signal phrases that indicate each pattern.

stage_projects.name: Binary Search Beyond Sorted Arrays
stage_projects.description: Solve 6 problems that use binary search in non-obvious ways (search on answer space, rotated arrays, first/last occurrence), documenting the invariant maintained in each solution.

stage_projects.name: Stock Trading Simulator via Kadane’s Variants
stage_projects.description: Solve the full family of "best time to buy/sell stock" problems (I through IV) building from basic Kadane’s to the DP-augmented versions with transaction limits, with a written explanation of how each variant extends the last.

stage_projects.name: Expression Evaluator
stage_projects.description: Build a calculator that evaluates infix mathematical expressions with correct operator precedence and parentheses using a stack-based approach (shunting-yard or recursive descent), tested against 20 hand-crafted tricky expressions. Solve 6 monotonic stack problems (next greater element family, daily temperatures, largest rectangle in histogram), with a written template for recognizing when a monotonic stack applies.

stage_projects.name: Maze & Graph Explorer Toolkit
stage_projects.description: Solve a set of grid-based BFS/DFS problems (number of islands, rotting oranges, word ladder) with a shared, reusable grid-traversal helper function. Implement every classic tree traversal (in/pre/post-order, level-order) both recursively and iteratively, plus tree construction from traversal pairs, serialization/deserialization, and LCA — packaged as a small reusable tree utility module with tests.

stage_projects.name: Cycle Detection Across Data Structures
stage_projects.description: Implement Floyd’s Cycle Detection (tortoise and hare) applied to 3 different contexts: a linked list, an implicit "functional graph" (array where value = next index), and duplicate-number detection — documenting the shared mathematical insight across all three.

stage_projects.name: 1D DP Warm-Up Set
stage_projects.description: Solve 6 classic 1D DP problems (climbing stairs, house robber, coin change, longest increasing subsequence) implementing each with both memoization (top-down) and tabulation (bottom-up), comparing code clarity and space usage. Solve 8 2D DP problems (unique paths, edit distance, longest common subsequence, 0/1 knapsack) with a written "DP state design" note for each: what does dp[i][j] represent, and why.

stage_projects.name: DP Optimization Showcase
stage_projects.description: Take 3 of your 2D DP solutions and optimize their space complexity from O(n²) to O(n) using rolling arrays, documenting the transformation reasoning and benchmarking actual memory usage before/after on large inputs.

stage_projects.name: System Design Interview Playbook
stage_projects.description: Produce full written system design solutions (with diagrams) for 4 classic prompts (URL shortener, rate limiter, news feed, chat system) following a consistent framework: requirements clarification, capacity estimation, high-level design, deep dive, bottleneck/scaling discussion. Domain: systems design / interview prep.

stage_projects.name: Cache-Aside API Layer
stage_projects.description: Add Redis caching (via ioredis) to an earlier project’s read-heavy endpoints using the cache-aside pattern, with a documented cache-hit-rate measurement before/after and a sensible TTL/invalidation strategy per resource type. Domain: performance engineering.

stage_projects.name: Connection Pool Exhaustion Lab
stage_projects.description: Deliberately misconfigure PgBouncer to cause connection pool exhaustion under simulated load, observe and document the failure mode, then correctly configure pooling (transaction vs session mode) and prove the fix under the same load test. Domain: database infrastructure / SRE.

stage_projects.name: Serverless-Friendly Rate Limiter
stage_projects.description: Implement API rate limiting using Upstash (Redis-over-HTTP, works from serverless/edge functions) with @upstash/ratelimit, comparing sliding-window vs fixed-window algorithms with real traffic simulation. Domain: API infrastructure.

stage_projects.name: Branded Transactional Email System
stage_projects.description: Build a full transactional email flow (welcome, password reset, receipt) using React Email for templates (so emails are built with real component reuse) and Resend for delivery, tested across multiple email clients for rendering consistency. Domain: product/growth engineering.

stage_projects.name: Subscription Billing System
stage_projects.description: A full subscription billing integration with Razorpay: plan selection, checkout, webhook-based subscription-status sync (active/past-due/cancelled) back into your own database, and a customer-facing billing history page. Domain: fintech / SaaS billing. A one-time purchase flow (e.g., for a digital product) with Razorpay, including a documented refund process both via API and via the dashboard, and idempotent webhook handling so a duplicate webhook delivery never double-credits an order. Domain: e-commerce/fintech.

stage_projects.name: Request-Traceable Logging System
stage_projects.description: Add structured logging (pino) to an earlier API with a request ID propagated via AsyncLocalStorage through every log line of a request’s lifecycle, so any single request’s full log trail can be grepped by ID. Domain: observability / SRE.

stage_projects.name: Dual-Transport Logging Setup
stage_projects.description: Configure winston with two transports (console for dev, file/JSON for production) and demonstrate log-level filtering (debug locally, warn+ in production) driven by environment config. Domain: observability.

stage_projects.name: Production Error Triage Dashboard
stage_projects.description: Integrate Sentry into a full-stack app (both frontend and backend), including source maps for readable stack traces, user context attachment, and custom error grouping/tagging for a specific error-prone feature. Domain: SRE / observability. Set up UptimeRobot monitors for a deployed project’s critical endpoints and build a small public status page that reflects real uptime data. Domain: SRE / product trust.

stage_projects.name: Unified Observability Stack Comparison
stage_projects.description: Ship the same application’s logs to 3 different platforms in parallel (e.g., Better Stack, Axiom, and Grafana Cloud + Loki) and write a hands-on comparison covering query experience, retention/pricing, and alerting capability. Domain: infrastructure decision-making.

stage_projects.name: CloudWatch-Based AWS Monitoring Setup
stage_projects.description: For any component deployed with AWS involvement, configure CloudWatch log groups, metric filters, and a basic alarm (e.g., error-rate spike) that would page a real on-call engineer. Domain: AWS/SRE.

stage_projects.name: Feature-Flagged A/B Pricing Experiment
stage_projects.description: Run a real (or realistic simulated) A/B test on a pricing page using PostHog feature flags to split traffic, tracked through to a conversion event, with statistical significance discussed in a written results report. Domain: growth engineering / experimentation. Use funnel analysis and session recordings to identify the exact step where users abandon an onboarding flow, propose and implement a fix, then re-measure the funnel to validate improvement. Domain: product/UX engineering.

stage_projects.name: Peer-to-Peer Video Chat
stage_projects.description: A 1:1 video call app using WebRTC with a signaling server (over WebSockets), including screen-share support and graceful handling of connection failures/ICE negotiation issues. Domain: communication tools.

stage_projects.name: Materialized View Reporting Dashboard
stage_projects.description: Build a reporting dashboard backed by materialized views for expensive aggregate queries (e.g., daily sales rollups), with a documented refresh strategy (scheduled vs on-demand) and a before/after query-time comparison vs. querying raw tables directly.

stage_projects.name: MVCC Behavior Demonstration Lab
stage_projects.description: A hands-on demo (two concurrent psql sessions) that reproduces and documents MVCC behavior: a long-running transaction not seeing another session’s committed changes, then explains what VACUUM is cleaning up afterward, with pg_stat_activity screenshots showing the live transaction state.

stage_projects.name: Read Replica Lag Simulation
stage_projects.description: Set up a primary + read replica PostgreSQL setup (locally via Docker), write to primary, read from replica, and deliberately induce and measure replication lag under write load, documenting a strategy for handling read-after-write consistency issues in application code.

stage_projects.name: Instant Search-As-You-Type with Meilisearch
stage_projects.description: A product catalog with typo-tolerant, sub-50ms instant search using Meilisearch, including faceted filtering (category, price range) synced from the primary database. Domain: e-commerce.

stage_projects.name: Search Engine Bake-Off
stage_projects.description: Index the identical dataset (e.g., 50k products) into Postgres full-text search, Typesense, and Elasticsearch, then benchmark query latency, relevance quality, and typo tolerance across all three with a written recommendation for different use-case scales. Domain: search infrastructure / platform engineering.

stage_projects.name: Multi-Provider Prompt Playground
stage_projects.description: A small internal tool that sends the same prompt to both the OpenAI API (GPT-4o) and the Anthropic API side-by-side, displaying responses, latency, and token usage for comparison. Domain: AI tooling / evaluation.

stage_projects.name: Structured Support-Ticket Classifier
stage_projects.description: A backend service that classifies incoming support tickets (category, urgency, sentiment) using an LLM API call, with proper error handling for API failures/timeouts and a fallback rule-based classifier if the API is unavailable. Domain: customer support automation.

stage_projects.name: Semantic Duplicate Detector
stage_projects.description: A tool that embeds a set of support tickets or forum posts (text-embedding-3-small) and finds semantic duplicates/near-duplicates using cosine similarity in pgvector, catching duplicates that keyword search would miss. Domain: content moderation / support tooling.

stage_projects.name: HNSW vs IVFFlat Benchmark
stage_projects.description: Index the same 100k-vector embedding set with both IVFFlat and HNSW in pgvector, benchmarking query latency and recall accuracy tradeoffs at different index parameters, with a written recommendation document. Domain: vector search infrastructure.

stage_projects.name: Multi-Document Research Assistant with Chunking Strategy Comparison
stage_projects.description: A RAG pipeline over a corpus of long-form documents (e.g., legal or research PDFs) that compares 3 different chunking strategies (fixed-size, semantic, sliding-window-with-overlap) on retrieval quality for the same question set, with a written evaluation report. Domain: legal-tech / research tooling.

stage_projects.name: Streaming AI Chat UI
stage_projects.description: A chat interface using the Vercel AI SDK with true token-by-token streaming responses, stop/regenerate controls, and conversation history persistence. Domain: AI product UX. A system where users submit a batch of documents for AI summarization; jobs are queued in BullMQ (not processed synchronously in the request), with a Bull Board dashboard for monitoring job status, retries, and failures. Domain: AI infrastructure / batch processing.

stage_projects.name: Cost-Optimized Multi-Tier Support Bot
stage_projects.description: A support bot that routes simple questions to a smaller/cheaper Claude model tier and escalates complex questions to a larger tier, with prompt caching applied to the large, static system prompt/knowledge base portion to cut repeated-request cost. Domain: AI cost engineering.

stage_projects.name: Receipt-to-Structured-Data Extractor
stage_projects.description: A tool that takes a photo/text of a receipt and uses tool calling to extract guaranteed-valid structured JSON (line items, totals, tax) validated against a schema, with a test suite of malformed/tricky receipts. Domain: fintech / expense automation.

stage_projects.name: Cost-Aware Multi-Model Router
stage_projects.description: A routing layer that sends each incoming request to the cheapest model capable of handling it correctly (classified by a lightweight pre-check), falling back to a stronger model on low-confidence responses, with logged cost savings versus an always-use-the-best-model baseline. Domain: AI infrastructure / cost engineering.

stage_projects.name: Prompt Version Control & Regression Suite
stage_projects.description: A system prompt library with versioned prompts and an automated eval suite (a fixed set of test inputs with expected-quality criteria) that runs on every prompt change to catch regressions before deploying a new prompt version. Domain: AI engineering / MLOps.

stage_projects.name: Eval-Driven Support Bot Improvement Cycle
stage_projects.description: Take the Stage 5 support bot, build a 30-example golden eval dataset with graded expected outputs, establish a baseline score, then iterate on the system prompt 3 times, re-running the eval each time and documenting the score progression and specific failure modes fixed. Domain: AI quality engineering.

stage_projects.name: Local-First Bookmark Manager with Sync
stage_projects.description: A bookmark manager storing data primarily in IndexedDB with a background sync-to-server layer, handling the case where local and server data diverge while offline, including a documented conflict-resolution strategy. Domain: productivity tools.

stage_projects.name: CPU-Heavy Data Processing Without UI Freeze
stage_projects.description: A tool that processes a large CSV/JSON file (parsing, aggregation) entirely inside a Web Worker using comlink for clean async communication, keeping the UI thread responsive throughout — with a visible before/after (UI freezes without the worker, doesn’t with it).

stage_projects.name: Cross-Tab Session Sync
stage_projects.description: A demo app where logging out in one browser tab immediately logs the user out in all other open tabs of the same app, using the Broadcast Channel API. Domain: security/session management UX.

stage_projects.name: Native Page Transition Gallery
stage_projects.description: A multi-page image gallery using the View Transitions API for smooth native page-to-page morph animations (image expanding into a detail view), with a custom CSS Houdini paint worklet used for one decorative element (e.g., a custom-drawn border or background pattern). Domain: creative/media portfolios.

stage_projects.name: Offline-Capable Collaborative Doc with Peer Fallback
stage_projects.description: A collaborative text document combining y-indexeddb (offline persistence), y-websocket (primary sync via a Hocuspocus server), and y-webrtc as a peer-to-peer fallback when the server is unreachable, demonstrating that edits made offline merge correctly once any sync path reconnects. Domain: collaborative software infrastructure.

stage_projects.name: Notion-Style Block Editor
stage_projects.description: A rich text editor built with Tiptap (on ProseMirror) supporting headings, lists, code blocks, and a custom block type you build yourself (e.g., an embeddable "callout" box), with full keyboard shortcuts and markdown-style input rules (typing "# " converts to a heading). Domain: productivity / content tools. Integrate Tiptap with Yjs for real-time collaborative rich-text editing with live cursors showing collaborator names/colors — a genuine Google-Docs-style editing experience built from open primitives. Domain: collaborative software.

stage_projects.name: API Breaking Point Report
stage_projects.description: Use k6 to load-test an earlier project’s API, ramping virtual users until it breaks, and produce a written report identifying the exact bottleneck (CPU, DB connections, memory) with graphs. Domain: performance engineering / SRE. Run a distributed load test from multiple geographic regions using k6 Cloud, comparing latency experienced by users in different regions and documenting a CDN/edge-caching recommendation based on findings.

stage_projects.name: Realistic User-Behavior Load Simulation with Artillery
stage_projects.description: Model a realistic multi-step user journey (browse → search → add to cart → checkout) as an Artillery scenario with weighted random behavior (not just hammering one endpoint), simulating a realistic traffic spike (e.g., a flash sale) and documenting system behavior under it.

stage_projects.name: Automated Vulnerability Scanning Pipeline
stage_projects.description: Integrate OWASP ZAP into a CI pipeline to automatically scan a staging deployment on every merge, failing the build on high-severity findings. Domain: DevSecOps.

stage_projects.name: Nonce-Based CSP Hardening
stage_projects.description: Implement a strict, nonce-based Content Security Policy on a real app (no unsafe-inline), correctly generating a fresh nonce per request and wiring it through server-rendered script tags, verified with a CSP evaluator and a deliberate XSS-attempt test that gets blocked.

stage_projects.name: Secret Leak Prevention Pipeline
stage_projects.description: Configure trufflehog and git-secrets to scan every commit (locally via pre-commit hook and in CI) for accidentally committed secrets, with a deliberate test commit containing a fake API key that gets correctly blocked.

stage_projects.name: Continuous Security Posture Dashboard
stage_projects.description: A small internal report generator that runs securityheaders.com checks, CSP Evaluator, npm audit, and summarizes Dependabot alert status for a project into a single weekly security posture report. Domain: DevSecOps.

stage_projects.name: SOC 2 & GDPR Readiness Checklist Implementation
stage_projects.description: Produce a real, project-specific SOC 2-informed security control checklist and GDPR data-handling checklist for an earlier project, then implement the 5 highest-priority gaps found (e.g., access logging, data export/deletion endpoints) rather than just documenting them. Domain: compliance / security engineering.

stage_projects.name: Framework-Free Vite App from Scratch
stage_projects.description: Configure a Vite project from an empty folder (no create-vite scaffold) with TypeScript, path aliases, and environment variable handling, understanding every config option added. Domain: build tooling literacy.

stage_projects.name: Dual-Format Publishable Library with tsup
stage_projects.description: Take a utility library from Phase 1/4 and configure tsup to build it as both ESM and CJS output with generated type declarations, ready for real npm publishing. Domain: library authoring / open source.

stage_projects.name: Bundle Size Audit & Diet
stage_projects.description: Take a real project, run @next/bundle-analyzer (or vite-bundle-visualizer for non-Next projects), identify the 3 largest unnecessary dependencies or duplicated code, and reduce total bundle size by a documented, measurable percentage.

stage_projects.name: Themeable Component Library, Three Ways
stage_projects.description: Rebuild the same 4-component set using styled-components, Emotion, and Linaria (zero-runtime) respectively, then write a hands-on comparison of DX, runtime performance cost, and SSR complexity for each. Domain: frontend architecture decision-making.

stage_projects.name: Direct-to-S3 Upload System
stage_projects.description: A file upload feature using pre-signed S3 URLs so large files upload directly from the browser to S3 (not proxied through your server), with upload progress tracking and correct bucket policy/CORS configuration. Domain: media/file storage infrastructure.

stage_projects.name: Terraform Security Scan Gate
stage_projects.description: Integrate tfsec into a CI pipeline that scans Terraform plans for security misconfigurations (e.g., a publicly-open security group) before allowing an apply, with a deliberately insecure resource that gets correctly blocked.

stage_projects.name: Local Kubernetes Deployment

stage_projects.name: Zero-Downtime Rolling Update Demo
stage_projects.description: Configure a Kubernetes Deployment with proper readiness/liveness probes and rolling update strategy, then deploy a breaking change and demonstrate (with live traffic during the deploy) that users experience zero downtime, followed by a deliberately bad deploy that gets automatically rolled back.

stage_projects.name: Auto-Scaling Load Demonstration
stage_projects.description: Configure a Horizontal Pod Autoscaler on a deployed service, then load-test it (tying back to Phase 14’s k6 work) and record real pod-count scaling behavior as load increases and decreases.

stage_projects.name: Secure Secret Sync from Cloud Secret Manager
stage_projects.description: Configure external-secrets to sync secrets from a cloud secret manager (or a compatible local equivalent) into Kubernetes Secrets automatically, so no secret is ever manually kubectl-applied or committed anywhere.

stage_projects.name: Optimistic Social Feed
stage_projects.description: A social-media-style feed where likes/comments appear instantly (optimistic update) with correct rollback on simulated server rejection, backed by a cache-aside and a write-through caching strategy compared side-by-side on two different data types in the same app.

stage_projects.name: Idempotent Payment Retry Handler
stage_projects.description: A payment processing endpoint that safely handles duplicate/retried requests (e.g., a client retrying after a timeout) using an idempotency key, proven with a test that fires the same request 10 times concurrently and confirms only one charge occurs.

stage_projects.name: Order Fulfillment Saga
stage_projects.description: Model a multi-step order fulfillment process (charge payment → reserve inventory → schedule shipping) as a Saga with proper compensating transactions for each step, demonstrated by deliberately failing the shipping step and proving payment gets correctly refunded and inventory released.

stage_projects.name: Resilient Event-Driven Order Pipeline
stage_projects.description: The same order pipeline rebuilt using the Outbox pattern (to guarantee at-least-once event publishing alongside the DB transaction), a Dead Letter Queue for messages that repeatedly fail processing, and a Circuit Breaker around a flaky downstream shipping-provider API call.

stage_projects.name: CQRS-Based Reporting System
stage_projects.description: Split a write-heavy transactional data model from a read-optimized reporting model using CQRS — writes go through a normalized command model, reads are served from a denormalized, eventually-consistent query model — with documented consistency-lag behavior.

stage_projects.name: Row-Level Multi-Tenant SaaS Data Layer
stage_projects.description: Implement multi-tenancy for a SaaS app using a shared-database, row-level isolation strategy (tenant_id on every table + enforced query scoping), with a deliberate test proving one tenant can never see another tenant’s data even under a crafted malicious query attempt.

stage_projects.name: Chaos Engineering Game Day
stage_projects.description: Run a real chaos engineering exercise against one of your deployed systems: deliberately kill a service instance, inject network latency, or fail a dependency mid-request, and document what broke, what didn’t, and what you fixed afterward. Domain: SRE / resilience engineering.

stage_projects.name: Semantic-Release-Ready Open Source Package
stage_projects.description: Publish a real npm package (one of your earlier utility libraries) with Changesets managing version bumps and changelogs, wired into CI so merging a changeset automatically publishes a new version. Domain: open source maintenance.

stage_projects.name: Architecture Decision Record Backfill
stage_projects.description: Go back through 3 major decisions made earlier in this roadmap (e.g., "why Zustand over Redux," "why row-level multi-tenancy over schema-per-tenant") and write proper retroactive ADRs for each, following a consistent template (context, decision, consequences, alternatives considered).

stage_projects.name: RFC for a Real Architecture Change
stage_projects.description: Write a full RFC proposing a genuine architectural change to one of your existing projects (e.g., migrating from REST to GraphQL, or adding multi-region support), including alternatives considered and a rollout plan, as if presenting to a real engineering team.

stage_projects.name: Personal DORA Metrics Tracker
stage_projects.description: A small tool/dashboard that tracks your own deployment frequency, lead time for changes, change failure rate, and time to restore across this roadmap’s projects, pulled from real Git/CI history, not estimated.

stage_projects.name: Blameless Post-Mortem for a Real Bug
stage_projects.description: Write a full blameless post-mortem for a real bug or outage you caused somewhere in this roadmap (there will be one), following a proper template: timeline, impact, root cause, contributing factors, and concrete action items.

stage_projects.name: Portfolio-to-Application Pipeline
stage_projects.description: A polished, professional profile presence across Wellfound, Instahyre, and LinkedIn, each tailored to its audience (startup-focused vs. broad), all linking back to a coherent personal portfolio site showcasing this roadmap’s best 4–5 capstone projects with real metrics (not just screenshots).

Implement a user data deletion endpoint (GDPR "right to erasure") including a documented approach for data that must be retained (e.g., financial records).
Write a SOC 2-style access control policy for who can access production data and under what conditions.
Configure Vite path aliases (@/components) from scratch and verify both dev server and production build resolve them correctly.
Build a library with tsup producing both .mjs and .cjs outputs, and write a small test importing it both ways.
Add an environment-variable-driven feature flag to a Vite app and verify it’s correctly excluded from production if disabled.
Run a bundle analyzer on a real project and identify one dependency that’s larger than expected.
Replace one heavy dependency with a lighter alternative (or a hand-written equivalent) and measure the bundle size reduction.
Use rollup-plugin-visualizer on a Vite-built library to find and eliminate duplicate code across chunks.
Configure lighthouse-ci with a performance budget and prove a deliberately bloated asset triggers a CI failure.
Fix a real Lighthouse-flagged issue (e.g., unused CSS, unoptimized image) and confirm the score improves in a rerun.
Build a themeable Button in styled-components using a ThemeProvider.
Build the same Button in Emotion using the css prop and compare the authoring experience.
Build the same Button in Linaria and measure whether any runtime CSS-in-JS cost was actually eliminated (check the compiled output).
Generate a pre-signed S3 upload URL server-side and successfully upload a file directly from the browser using it.
Configure an S3 bucket policy that allows public read on one prefix but denies it on another, and verify both behaviors.
Implement upload progress tracking for a large file upload directly to S3.
Write a Terraform module provisioning at least 2 related cloud resources (e.g., a database + a storage bucket) with proper variable inputs and outputs.
Set up remote state in Terraform Cloud and demonstrate a teammate-simulated workflow: plan, review, apply.
Run tfsec against a deliberately misconfigured resource (public S3 bucket) and confirm it’s flagged, then fix it.
Deploy a simple app to a kind cluster and expose it via a Service, accessing it from your local browser.
Write a ConfigMap and Secret, and mount both correctly into a running Pod.
Configure a readiness probe and prove a Pod that fails it never receives traffic.
Trigger a rolling update and observe (via kubectl get pods -w) the old and new pods transitioning without a traffic gap.
Package an app as a Helm chart with at least 3 configurable values and install it twice with different value sets.
Configure an HPA with a CPU threshold, generate load with k6, and record the pod count scaling up and back down.
Set up external-secrets to sync one secret automatically and prove a manually-deleted Kubernetes Secret gets recreated by the operator.
Implement an optimistic update for a "like" action and simulate a server rejection, proving the UI correctly reverts.
Implement write-through caching for a frequently-updated resource and explain, in writing, why it was chosen over cache-aside for that specific resource.
Implement optimistic locking with a version column and prove a concurrent conflicting update is correctly rejected.
Implement pessimistic locking with SELECT FOR UPDATE and prove concurrent transactions serialize correctly instead of racing.
Implement idempotency-key handling for a POST endpoint and prove 10 concurrent identical requests produce exactly one side effect.
Implement a 3-step Saga with compensating transactions and prove a mid-sequence failure correctly unwinds prior steps.
Implement the Outbox pattern and prove an event is never lost even if the message broker is briefly unavailable at commit time.
Implement a Circuit Breaker around an unreliable API call and prove it opens after repeated failures and half-opens to test recovery.
Route a message that fails processing 3 times into a Dead Letter Queue and build a small tool to inspect/replay DLQ messages.
Add a new event consumer to an existing event-driven system without touching the publisher’s code.
Build a CQRS read model that is intentionally eventually-consistent, and write a test that tolerates (and documents) that lag.
Add tenant-scoped row-level security (via ORM middleware or DB-level RLS) and prove a cross-tenant data leak is impossible even if a developer forgets a WHERE clause.
Write a migration strategy document for moving a single-tenant schema to multi-tenant without data loss.
Execute a blue-green deployment and switch traffic with zero dropped requests (verified via a continuous request script running during the switch).
Kill a running service instance under load and document exactly how the system behaved (did it recover, how long did it take, did users notice).
Inject artificial latency into one dependency and observe whether your Circuit Breaker (Stage 3) correctly protects the rest of the system.
Add Changesets to an existing library, create a changeset for a real change, and generate the resulting version bump and changelog entry.
Configure CI to auto-publish on changeset merge and verify a real version lands on npm (or a local/private registry).
Write one ADR for a decision you made without documentation earlier in this roadmap.
Write one RFC proposing a change you have not yet implemented, and get feedback (self-critique or peer) before "approving" it.
Calculate your own deployment frequency and lead time for changes from real Git history of one project.
Write a blameless post-mortem for a real incident, ensuring the language focuses on systems/process, not individual blame.
Create a Technical Debt Tracking log for one project and prioritize the top 5 items by impact vs. effort.
Track estimated vs. actual time for 5 tasks from this roadmap and write a short reflection on your estimation accuracy.
Write a short Code Review Conventions doc reflecting standards you’ve actually been applying to your own PRs.
Write an ARCHITECTURE.md for a real project including at least one Mermaid system diagram.
Set up a docs/adr/ folder with at least 3 numbered, properly formatted ADRs.
Write a MONITORING.md documenting every alert configured for a real project and what each one means operationally.
Write an OPERATIONS.md with step-by-step deploy and rollback instructions precise enough for someone else to follow blind.
Write 5 PRODUCT_DECISIONS.md entries justifying real UX/product choices from an earlier project.

capstones.name: DevScribe
capstones.title: A Personal Developer Journal & Snippet Manager
capstones.description: Build a complete, deployable application that: is scaffolded with a proper dotfiles-provisioned dev environment (Stage 1); has full semantic, accessible HTML structure (Stage 2); is responsively styled with hand-written CSS Grid/Flexbox, no framework (Stage 3); implements all core logic in strict TypeScript compiled from scratch, covering async data fetching from a raw Node http server, custom iterators for browsing entries, a Proxy-based reactive UI updater, Web Worker-based full-text search indexing, and IndexedDB or a JSON file store for persistence (Stages 4–5); uses a real SQL database (SQLite is fine) with a normalized schema for entries/tags/snippets and at least 3 non-trivial analytical queries (Stage 6); and is version-controlled with clean Conventional Commit history, a CONTRIBUTING.md, linting, and a documented Git workflow (Stage 7). Deliverable: a working local-first journal/snippet app plus a written architecture doc explaining every technical decision. Domain: developer productivity tools. Why it matters: this project alone demonstrates command of the entire JS/TS/SQL/Git foundation without leaning on any framework crutch.

capstones.name: CivicBoard
capstones.title: A Server-Rendered Local Government Issue Tracker
capstones.description: A full Next.js 15 App Router application where citizens report local issues (potholes, broken streetlights) and track status. Combines: static public pages for browsing resolved/open issues (ISR), a Server Action-powered report submission form, an authenticated admin dashboard behind middleware with parallel routes (queue / map view / stats), intercepting routes for a "quick view" issue modal, edge-personalized location defaults, and a deployed, benchmarked production build on Vercel with documented caching strategy per route. Domain: civic tech. Why it matters: this is a realistic, socially useful full-stack Next.js app that exercises nearly every App Router feature in one coherent product rather than in isolation.

capstones.name: Atlas
capstones.title: A Production-Grade, Multi-Brand Design System
capstones.description: Build a documented, installable component library (published as a local/private npm package) combining: a token pipeline (Style Dictionary) as the single source of truth, Tailwind and vanilla-extract both wired to consume those tokens, Radix-based accessible primitives styled with CVA, dark mode and multi-brand theming via next-themes/CSS variables, a schema-driven dynamic form system using react-hook-form \+ Zod, and a hand-built documentation/catalog page showing every component in every variant and theme. Domain: design systems / platform engineering. Why it matters: design systems are one of the highest-leverage, most portfolio-impressive artifacts a front-end engineer can build — this project proves you can architect one, not just consume one.

capstones.name: Pulse
capstones.title: A Real-Time Support Ticket Dashboard
capstones.description: A support-ticket triage dashboard combining every Phase 4 concept: Zustand for UI-local state (filters, selected ticket), TanStack Query \+ tRPC for fully type-safe server state with optimistic status updates and rollback, an XState machine governing the ticket lifecycle (new → assigned → in-progress → resolved → reopened) with guards preventing invalid transitions, Suspense \+ error boundaries per panel so one broken widget never takes down the dashboard, Intersection/ResizeObserver-driven responsive charts, and a virtualized ticket list handling 50,000+ rows without jank, profiled and documented. Domain: customer support / SaaS operations tooling. Why it matters: this is a realistic "senior front-end engineer" artifact — the kind of dashboard that separates people who know individual libraries from people who can architect a resilient, performant system out of them.

capstones.name: Ledger
capstones.title: A Secure Multi-Tenant Expense-Approval API
capstones.description: A production-grade backend for a B2B expense-approval SaaS: hand-rolled Express architecture with layered middleware, a normalized multi-tenant PostgreSQL schema (via Prisma) supporting organizations/roles/approval chains, hardened with Helmet/CORS/rate-limiting/sanitization, a from-scratch JWT \+ httpOnly refresh-token auth system with rotation, HMAC-signed webhook endpoints for a simulated payment provider, comprehensive Supertest coverage (happy paths, auth failures, tampered webhooks), and a documented EXPLAIN ANALYZE-driven performance pass on the top 3 slowest endpoints under seeded load. Domain: fintech / B2B SaaS. Why it matters: this is a genuinely defensible "I built a secure backend" portfolio piece — covering real auth, real multi-tenancy, real hardening, not a tutorial CRUD app.

capstones.name: Shipwright
capstones.title: A Fully CI/CD-Automated, Containerized SaaS Deployment Pipeline
capstones.description: Take any earlier full-stack project (Phase 5’s "Ledger" is a good candidate) and build the complete professional delivery pipeline around it: Vitest \+ React Testing Library \+ MSW unit/component coverage with enforced thresholds, a Playwright E2E suite covering critical journeys across 3 browsers with visual regression checks, a multi-stage Dockerfile and docker-compose local dev environment, a full GitHub Actions pipeline (parallel lint/typecheck/test/E2E jobs, matrix-tested, cached, auto-publishing tagged images to GHCR on merge), and a live production deployment on Render with real status/coverage badges in the README. Domain: DevOps / release engineering. Why it matters: this is the artifact that proves you can ship software professionally, not just write it — the single most common gap between bootcamp-level and production-level engineers.

capstones.name: Nomad
capstones.title: An Offline-First Field Reporting App
capstones.description: A mobile app for field workers (e.g., inspectors, delivery drivers) who often lack connectivity: photo capture with camera permissions handled gracefully, offline-first data entry via AsyncStorage with a sync queue and conflict resolution on reconnect, secure token storage via expo-secure-store, push notifications for assignment updates, a FlatList-based large history view tuned for performance, multi-environment EAS build profiles, and a full store-submission-ready asset package plus at least one OTA update shipped to a test build. Domain: field service / logistics mobile tooling. Why it matters: offline-first, secure, store-ready mobile apps are a distinct and valuable skill set from web development — this proves end-to-end mobile shipping competence.

capstones.name: OpenGateway
capstones.title: A Fully Documented, Dual-Paradigm Public API Product
capstones.description: Take an existing backend (Phase 5’s "Ledger" works well) and ship it as a genuine API product: a complete hand-written OpenAPI 3.0 spec rendered via Swagger UI, Mermaid-diagrammed architecture and auth-flow documentation, a parallel GraphQL interface over the same data exposing at least one N+1-fixed resolver, a curated Postman collection with environments and auto-refreshing auth, and a written REST-vs-GraphQL decision document explaining which consumers should use which interface and why. Domain: developer platforms / API products. Why it matters: documenting and exposing an API well is a distinct, high-value skill from building it — this proves you can make your work usable by other engineers, not just functional.

capstones.name: Interview-Ready
capstones.title: A Personal DSA + System Design Reference System
capstones.description: Build a personal, structured knowledge base (could be a static site generated from markdown, tying back to Phase 1– 3 skills) cataloging: every pattern from Stages 1–6 with your own annotated solutions and a "recognize this pattern when..." cheat sheet per category, 4 fully written system design case studies with Mermaid architecture diagrams (tying back to Phase 7), and a log of at least 10 timed, REACTO-framework mock interviews with self-critique notes. Domain: career preparation / technical knowledge management. Why it matters: the artifact itself (a searchable, well-organized personal reference) is arguably more valuable long-term than any single solved problem — and building it forces genuine synthesis rather than passive practice.

capstones.name: Meridian
capstones.title: A Caching-Optimized SaaS Billing Backend
capstones.description: Extend Phase 5’s "Ledger" (or a similar backend) with: Redis cache-aside caching on the highest-traffic read endpoints with measured hit-rate improvements, PgBouncer correctly configured for connection pooling under load, Upstash-based edge-compatible rate limiting on public endpoints, a full React Email \+ Resend transactional email suite (welcome/receipt/billing-alert), and a complete Razorpay subscription billing integration with idempotent, signature-verified webhook handling syncing subscription state into the database. Domain: SaaS infrastructure / fintech. Why it matters: caching, email, and payments are the unglamorous plumbing every real SaaS product needs — getting them right (idempotency, cache invalidation, webhook security) is what separates hobby projects from production systems.

capstones.name: Watchtower
capstones.title: A Full Observability & Analytics Platform for a Production App
capstones.description: Wrap a complete observability and analytics layer around an earlier full-stack project: AsyncLocalStorage-propagated structured logging (pino) shipped to a real aggregation platform (Grafana Cloud \+ Loki), Sentry error tracking with source maps on both frontend and backend, UptimeRobot-backed public status page, full PostHog funnel instrumentation from landing to conversion with an active feature-flagged A/B experiment, session-recording-driven UX fixes with before/after funnel data, and a GDPR-compliant consent system that actually gates tracking. Domain: SRE / product analytics / privacy engineering. Why it matters: shipping a feature is half the job; knowing whether it works, why it breaks, and whether users actually use it is the other half — this project proves that operational maturity.

capstones.name: Concourse
capstones.title: A Real-Time Collaborative Marketplace with Enterprise-Grade Search
capstones.description: A live marketplace/auction-style platform combining: WebSocket-based real-time bidding with room-scoped broadcasts and an SSE-based public "live activity feed," a PostgreSQL schema tuned with composite and partial indexes validated via EXPLAIN ANALYZE, materialized-view-backed seller analytics dashboards, documented MVCC/replication behavior from a local primary+replica setup, and Elasticsearch-powered faceted, typo-tolerant listing search benchmarked against a Postgres full-text fallback. Domain: marketplace / e-commerce infrastructure. Why it matters: real-time interactivity and fast, relevant search are the two hardest-to-fake capabilities in consumer products — this project proves you can build both on solid database fundamentals, not just bolt on a SaaS widget.

capstones.name: Sage
capstones.title: A Cost-Governed, Eval-Tested RAG Support Platform
capstones.description: A complete production-pattern AI support platform: a documentation-grounded RAG pipeline (pgvector, chunking strategy chosen via comparison testing, citation tracking), a cost-optimized multi-tier Claude routing layer with prompt caching on the static knowledge base, tool-calling-based structured ticket extraction validated with Zod, BullMQ-queued background processing for bulk document ingestion with a Bull Board monitoring dashboard, a real-time AI cost dashboard with hard budget enforcement per organization, and a versioned prompt library backed by an automated golden-dataset eval suite that must pass before any prompt change ships. Domain: enterprise AI / support automation. Why it matters: this is what separates "called an LLM API" from "built a production AI system" — grounding, cost control, and evaluation discipline are the actual hard parts.

capstones.name: Confluence Lite
capstones.title: A Real-Time Collaborative Document Workspace
capstones.description: A Notion/Google-Docs-style collaborative workspace: a Tiptap-based rich text editor with custom block extensions, fully wired to Yjs for real-time collaborative editing (y-websocket primary sync via a Hocuspocus server, y-indexeddb for offline persistence, y-webrtc as a peer-to-peer fallback), live cursor presence, cross-tab session sync via Broadcast Channel, CPU-heavy operations (e.g., full-document search indexing) offloaded to a Web Worker via comlink so typing never lags, and smooth View-Transitions-powered navigation between documents. Domain: collaborative productivity software. Why it matters: real-time collaborative editing is one of the most technically demanding categories of web application — building a working version from open primitives (not a SaaS embed) is a genuine senior-level achievement.

capstones.name: Bastion
capstones.title: A Load-Tested, Security-Hardened Production Audit
capstones.description: A full offensive-and-defensive audit of an earlier full-stack project: k6 and Artillery load tests establishing real breaking points and p99 latency under realistic traffic simulation, a documented OWASP Top 10 self-audit with real vulnerabilities found and fixed, a nonce-based strict CSP and JWT algorithm pinning implemented and verified, automated secret scanning wired into CI, a continuous security-header/dependency-audit reporting pipeline, and a GDPR-compliant data export/deletion implementation backed by a written SOC 2-informed access control policy. Domain: application security / SRE. Why it matters: this is the project that proves you don’t just build features — you can find out where your own system breaks and where it’s vulnerable, and actually fix it, which is precisely what separates confident production engineers from tutorial-followers.

capstones.name: Featherweight
capstones.title: A Bundle-Size-Obsessed Component Library
capstones.description: Publish a small, genuinely optimized component library: authored and bundled with tsup (dual ESM/CJS \+ types), a documented before/after bundle-size reduction case study using bundle analyzers, a CI pipeline enforcing a Lighthouse performance budget on the accompanying demo site, and a written comparative report on styled-components vs. Emotion vs. Linaria implementations of the same components with real measured runtime cost differences. Domain: frontend performance / library engineering. Why it matters: most engineers never measure what their styling/build choices actually cost; this project builds the habit of verifying performance claims with real numbers instead of assumptions.

capstones.name: Foundry
capstones.title: A Fully Terraform-and-Kubernetes-Managed Production Platform
capstones.description: Take an earlier full-stack project and rebuild its entire infrastructure as code: S3 pre-signed direct uploads for media, all cloud resources defined in Terraform with tfsec-gated CI and Terraform Cloud remote state, the application itself packaged as a Helm chart deployed to Kubernetes with readiness/liveness probes enabling zero-downtime rolling updates, a Horizontal Pod Autoscaler validated under real k6 load, and external-secrets syncing all credentials so nothing sensitive is ever manually applied. Domain: platform engineering / DevOps infrastructure. Why it matters: this is genuine platform-engineer-level work — reproducible, auditable infrastructure is what lets a team scale past "it works on the one server I set up manually."

capstones.name: Resilient Commerce
capstones.title: A Distributed, Multi-Tenant Order Platform
capstones.description: A multi-tenant e-commerce order platform combining every pattern in this phase: optimistic-locked inventory and idempotent payment handling preventing overselling and double-charges, a Saga-orchestrated fulfillment pipeline with the Outbox pattern for reliable event publishing, a Circuit Breaker and Dead Letter Queue protecting against a flaky shipping provider, an event-driven notification system decoupled via pub/sub, a CQRS-split reporting layer for seller analytics, strict row-level multi-tenant data isolation proven under adversarial testing, and a blue-green deployment pipeline validated with a real chaos engineering game day. Domain: e-commerce / distributed systems. Why it matters: this is the single most architecturally advanced project in the entire roadmap — it proves genuine distributed-systems thinking, not just feature-building.

capstones.name: Glasshouse
capstones.title: A Fully Documented, Publishable Engineering Portfolio Project
capstones.description: Take your single most impressive project from anywhere in this roadmap and bring its engineering craft to a publishable standard: a Changesets-managed, auto-published package extracted from its reusable internals, a complete ADR history and RFC for its next proposed evolution, real DORA metrics pulled from its Git/CI history, a blameless post-mortem for a genuine incident, and the full documentation set (ARCHITECTURE.md, DECISIONS.md, PERFORMANCE.md, SECURITY.md, MONITORING.md, OPERATIONS.md, TECH\\\_DEBT.md, PRODUCT\\\_DECISIONS.md) written to a standard where a stranger engineer could fully onboard and operate it without ever talking to you. Domain: engineering craft / technical leadership. Why it matters: documentation and process discipline is what makes an individual’s work into an organization’s asset — this is the artifact that signals senior/staff-level maturity, not just coding ability.

capstones.name: Launch
capstones.title: A Complete Public Engineering Presence
capstones.description: Synthesize the entire roadmap into a real public footprint: a portfolio site (built with everything learned in Phases 1–3) showcasing your 5 strongest capstones with real architecture docs linked in, a genuine Product Hunt launch of your best project with measured traction, a 3-part technical article series published across dev.to and Hashnode documenting real lessons learned (load testing failures, security findings, architectural tradeoffs — not tutorials), and tailored, live profiles on LinkedIn/Wellfound/Instahyre driving toward real conversations. Domain: career development / developer relations. Why it matters: an extraordinary body of technical work that nobody knows about has zero career leverage — this final phase converts 1,159.5 hours of deep engineering work into a visible, credible, discoverable professional presence.

advanced_projects.name: TiffinOS
advanced_projects.problem: India has ~500,000 home-based tiffin/dabba services. A typical operator manages 50–200 customers, 2–3 delivery boys, daily menus, dietary preferences, subscription pauses, UPI payments, and monthly renewals — entirely on WhatsApp and paper. Swiggy and Zomato don't solve this. They compete with it.
advanced_projects.who_exactly: Amma running a tiffin service from her kitchen in Koramangala, Bangalore. 80 customers. 2 delivery boys. Currently: WhatsApp groups, handwritten ledger, GPay screenshots in an album.
advanced_projects.what_exists: Nothing affordable. NoBrokerHood and similar apps are for housing societies. Zoho is too heavy. Tiffin operators don't know what SaaS is — they need something that feels like WhatsApp but runs their business.
advanced_projects.the_gap: Subscription management + route optimization + WhatsApp-native notifications + UPI recurring billing in one tool priced at ₹499/month.
core_features: Customer subscription management (start, pause, resume, cancel)
Daily menu upload with photo (customers see it via web link)
Delivery boy mobile PWA with offline support
Route optimization (which buildings to hit in which order per area)
UPI/Razorpay subscription with auto-renewal
Monthly statement generation per customer
advanced_features: Dietary preference engine — no onion, no garlic, Jain, diabetic — auto-flags when menu conflicts with customer preference
WhatsApp Business API integration — delivery confirmation, payment reminder, menu of the day — all via WhatsApp without the operator doing anything manually
Delivery proof — delivery boy clicks photo at doorstep, timestamped, geo-tagged, sent to customer automatically
Subscription health dashboard — churn rate, average subscription length, peak pause months, revenue forecast
Customer self-service portal — customer logs in, pauses their own subscription, changes address, views their own payment history
Multi-branch support — operator with 2 kitchens in different areas manages both from one dashboard
P&L per month — ingredients cost (manual input) vs revenue = profit margin per month

skill_mapping.feature: PWA with offline delivery boy app

advanced_projects.monetization: ₹499/month per tiffin service. 100 customers = ₹49,900 MRR. Land and expand.
advanced_projects.first_users: Walk into any residential area in Bangalore and ask who delivers tiffin. Every apartment complex has 2–3. Offer free first month.

advanced_projects.name: BatchIQ
advanced_projects.problem: India has 1.5 million coaching institutes. 90% are small (10–500 students). They manage batches, attendance, fee collection, test scores, and parent communication on Excel, WhatsApp, and paper registers. Extramarks and similar tools cost ₹2–5 LPA and are built for large institutes. Small coaching institutes have nothing.
advanced_projects.who_exactly: A JEE coaching teacher in Rajajinagar, Bangalore running 3 batches of 40 students each. Collects fees manually. Tracks attendance on a register. WhatsApps test scores to parents individually.
advanced_projects.what_exists: Extramarks, Teachmint (shut down free tier), ClassPlus. All either too expensive or too feature-bloated for small operators.
advanced_projects.the_gap: A lightweight, affordable (₹999/month) institute manager that a single teacher can set up in one afternoon.
core_features: Batch and student management
Attendance marking (teacher marks per class)
Fee collection tracker with defaulter list
Test score entry and report card generation
Automated WhatsApp/SMS to parents on fee due, test results, attendance
advanced_features: AI weak topic detector — based on 3+ test scores, identifies which chapters a student consistently underperforms in and surfaces this to teacher and parent
Batch scheduler with conflict detection — teacher tries to schedule Physics batch on Monday 5 PM but already has Chemistry at that time — system blocks and suggests alternatives
Fee defaulter escalation flow — 7 days overdue: WhatsApp reminder. 15 days: call reminder task assigned to admin. 30 days: batch access restricted automatically
Parent portal — parent sees child's attendance %, test scores, fee due date, upcoming exams — no WhatsApp needed
Study material distribution — teacher uploads PDF notes, only students in that batch can access — not shared publicly
Performance prediction — based on test score trajectory and attendance, predicts which students are at risk of failing the final exam (logistic regression, not deep ML)
Teacher salary calculator — if teacher is paid per class taken, system calculates monthly salary based on attendance register
Exam countdown dashboard — visible to students: days left to JEE/NEET, daily study targets
advanced_projects.monetization: ₹999/month per institute. Freemium: up to 30 students free. Upsell: AI features at ₹1,999/month.
advanced_projects.first_users: Every residential neighbourhood has 3–5 tuition centres. Walk in. Show a live demo. Offer free setup.

advanced_projects.name: QueueMD
advanced_projects.tagline: Clinic Queue and Patient Management System
advanced_projects.problem: 80% of small private clinics in India still use paper tokens. Patients arrive, get a number, sit for 2–3 hours with no idea of their position. The clinic has no data on wait times, peak hours, or no-shows. Practo solves this for large clinics. Small single-doctor clinics (which are everywhere) have nothing.
advanced_projects.who_exactly: Dr. Sharma running a general physician clinic in Indiranagar. 40–60 patients per day. Paper token system. Receptionist manually calls out numbers. No data. No visibility for patients.
advanced_projects.what_exists: Practo (expensive, complex), Lybrate (patient-facing booking, not clinic management). Nothing lightweight for the operator side.
advanced_projects.the_gap: A ₹799/month system that replaces the paper token with a real-time queue, WhatsApp updates to patients, and a dashboard the doctor can glance at between consultations.
core_features: Digital token issuance (patient scans QR at reception or walks in)
Real-time queue display (TV mode for waiting area)
Doctor console (see queue, call next, mark done, skip)
WhatsApp notification when patient is 3 numbers away
Basic patient record (name, phone, reason for visit)
Daily analytics (patients seen, avg wait time, peak hour)
advanced_features: AI triage — patient enters symptoms at check-in, system estimates priority (routine/urgent/emergency) and suggests queue position to receptionist
Appointment slots + walk-in hybrid — some slots reserved for pre-booked, rest for walk-ins — balanced queue management
Patient history — returning patients linked by phone number, doctor sees last 5 visits in one click
No-show prediction — based on past data, flags patients who historically no-show and automatically overbooks those slots
Multi-doctor routing — clinic has 2 doctors, patient selects doctor or gets auto-assigned based on queue load
Prescription builder — doctor types diagnosis + medicines, system generates a printable prescription (with clinic letterhead) — not meant to replace EMR, just the paper prescription
Lab result upload — patient's blood test PDF uploaded, linked to their record, sent to their WhatsApp
Monthly clinic report — total patients, revenue estimate (if fee is tracked), busiest days, most common complaints
advanced_projects.monetization: ₹799/month per clinic. Hardware upsell: pre-configured Raspberry Pi with queue display software (₹4,999 one-time).
advanced_projects.first_users: Stand outside any clinic and wait. Talk to the receptionist, not the doctor. Offer to set it up free for 30 days.

advanced_projects.name: TaxStack
advanced_projects.tagline: Freelancer GST + TDS + Advance Tax Manager
advanced_projects.problem: Indian freelancers (developers, designers, consultants) earning ₹5–50 LPA face a compliance nightmare: GST on services (18%), TDS deducted by clients (10%), quarterly advance tax payments, Form 26AS reconciliation, ITR filing. ClearTax solves the filing. Nobody solves the year-round tracking and estimation.

What This Document Is

This is a ~17.5-month, 290-topic, phase-based software engineering curriculum totaling 3034 realistic hours, designed to take you from a beginner to a job-ready full-stack engineer — with salaries at each Exit Point ranging ₹6–10 LPA at the earliest exit up to ₹35–50 LPA at the final one. It's structured as a self-study roadmap with built-in "Exit Points" — specific milestones where you're ready to start applying for jobs at different salary levels.

orientation.job_market_case:
Especially if you're a BCA graduate from a Tier‑2 college with zero projects and no work experience.

THE HONEST TRUTH – AND THE PLAN

The market is tough, but it's not closed. Companies still hire – they hire people who can ship code, not people with fancy degrees. This curriculum is designed to turn you into that person.

Here's how it works for you:

— You build a real, deployable project (ClientSync) in the first 6 months — this becomes your portfolio, your proof of skill, and your conversation starter in interviews.

— You publish your work publicly — every phase gives you something to show on GitHub, dev.to, or LinkedIn. Recruiters see your progress, not your college name.

— You don't wait until the end to apply — the 'Exit Points' let you start applying as early as Phase 06, when you have a live app and a CI/CD pipeline. That's often enough for early-stage startups.

— The curriculum explicitly addresses the BCA degree filter — it tells you which companies don't care about your degree (most startups, product companies, dev agencies) and which do (FAANG, large IT services). You focus your energy where it matters.

— You learn exactly what's needed for the job — no fluff, no outdated theory. Every topic is chosen because it's used in production at top startups. You're job-ready, not just 'certified'.

— You build in public — by the time you finish, you have a network, a trail of content, and often inbound interest from founders. That's how you beat the 'no experience' trap.

THE BOTTOM LINE

Your BCA degree is not a blocker – it's a starting point. What gets you hired is your ability to build and ship. This roadmap gives you the exact path to do that, with clear milestones to keep you on track.

If you follow it consistently, you will have a portfolio, a GitHub history, and the confidence to walk into any interview. The jobs are there – you just need to be visible and credible. This document shows you how.
orientation.build_in_public_guide:
"Build in public" gets said so often it's stopped meaning anything. Here's what it actually means for this roadmap: at the end of most phases (not every day, not every commit), you post one specific, concrete thing you built or learned — not a status update, not "day 47 of my coding journey." Each phase in this document has a compact BUILD IN PUBLIC callout telling you exactly what to post, what to commit, and where. This section is the reasoning behind that system.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN YOUR DEGREE

A recruiter or hiring manager cannot verify "I know React." They can verify a GitHub repo with real commit history, a deployed URL, a green CI badge, and a dev.to post that explains a real decision you made. Visibility isn't vanity here — it's the only evidence a stranger can check in 90 seconds. Silence is the default; everyone in this roadmap is building the same 20 phases. The difference between two people with identical skills is which one has proof.

GITHUB

* Commit as you go, not in one dump at the end of a phase. A commit history with 3 commits on the last day of every phase reads as fabricated. It probably is.

* Use Conventional Commits from Phase 04 onward (feat:, fix:, refactor:, etc.) — it's a topic in the curriculum for a reason; a recruiter who opens your commit log should see discipline, not noise.

* Every repo gets a real README: what it does, how to run it, what you learned. "TODO: add README" sitting untouched for months is a worse signal than no README at all.

* Pin your 2–3 best repos on your GitHub profile. Don't make someone dig through 40 repos to find the one that matters.

LINKEDIN

* Post when you ship something visible — a deployed feature, a working demo, a hard bug you fixed. Not "studying TypeScript today," which nobody can evaluate.

* Lead with what it does or looks like (a screenshot, a short screen-recording), not with the tech stack. Recruiters skim; a visual gets 2 seconds of attention, a paragraph of jargon gets zero.

* One post per phase is enough. A LinkedIn feed with 40 low-effort posts is worse than one with 15 real ones — frequency without substance reads as noise, not progress.

DEV.TO / HASHNODE

* Write about a specific decision or a specific bug, never a tutorial recap of something already covered better elsewhere ("What is React?" gets you nothing — 500,000 of those already exist).

* The BUILD IN PUBLIC callouts flag which phases are worth a dev.to post and which aren't (Phase 08's DSA grind and Phase 15's build tooling aren't — skip posting, keep building).

* A post that says "here's a mistake I made and how I fixed it" outperforms one that says "here's how to do X correctly" — the former is credible because it's specific and honest; the latter reads as copied.

The rule underneath all of it: post less than you think you should, and make sure what you do post could survive someone actually clicking through. A thin GitHub history with real commits beats a loud one with none.

why_this_works.mechanism: Build in Public system — a required post/commit/README artifact at the end of every phase, not optional polish.

why_this_works.failure_mode: Waiting until the very end to apply for jobs
why_this_works.mechanism: Exit Points (A, B, ★1, C, ★2, D, 3, E) — real job-readiness milestones seeded from Phase 06 onward, each with its own target roles and salary band.

why_this_works.failure_mode: Learning topics before their prerequisites are solid
why_this_works.mechanism: Dependency-ordered resequencing — explicitly reasoned in-document (e.g. Type Narrowing before Discriminated Unions, HMAC-SHA256 before JWT, curl before Postman) rather than following the original curriculum’s grouping.
Weekly-hours-based timeline options (25–85 hrs/wk) with an explicit daily schedule and "track hours weekly, not daily" rule — a rough day doesn’t derail the plan.

why_this_works.failure_mode: A portfolio with no depth — one demo, no real product
why_this_works.mechanism: ClientSync — a single real, deployable, two-sided SaaS product built feature-by-feature across every phase, rather than 19 disconnected toy projects.

why_this_works.failure_mode: Degree/college filtering you out before anyone sees your work
why_this_works.mechanism: The document explicitly separates companies that gate on degree (FAANG India, large IT services) from those that don’t (most startups, product companies, dev agencies) — so effort is targeted, not wasted.

why_this_works.failure_mode: GitHub history that looks fabricated (a dump of commits at the last minute)
why_this_works.mechanism: Conventional Commits from Phase 04 onward + explicit guidance to commit as you go, not in one end-of-phase dump.

navigation.dsa_spine_index:
Phase 08 (DSA & Interview Preparation) is the single highest-leverage exit gate in the roadmap — the first point where you’re competitive in a full interview loop, not just portfolio review.

* **Precedes it:** Phases 01–07 (dev fundamentals, React/Next.js, UI, state management, backend/DB/auth, testing/CI/CD/deployment, API docs) — everything DSA patterns get layered onto.

* **Follows it:** Exit ★ 1 unlocked (Series A/B startups, product companies) — then Phases 09 onward build production-grade breadth (caching, payments, monitoring, real-time, AI, infra, architecture).
mvp_fast_path: Phases 01, 01b, 02, 03, 04, 05, 06 — in that order — reach Exit A at ~7.1 months (@40 hrs/wk).
Everything from Phase 07 onward extends the profile toward higher exits (B, ★ 1, C, ★ 2, D, 3, E) — not required to start applying.
